items.notes: Diagnosed 2026-11-25: the page has a raw 0xC2 byte before \[co] (Copyright \302\[co] 1999), invalid UTF-8. Our decode gives U+FFFD + ©, groff reads the byte as U+00C2 and prints Â©. Decide: refuse a page whose decode contains U+FFFD (faithful-or-refuse), or map invalid bytes Latin-1 like groff. Either moves the 4123 parsed / 27 refused count, so it is a decision, not a lane fix.

items.title: copy mode still reduces \. to "."; a body line starting with \. becomes an unknown request and refuses the page where groff prints nothing
items.notes: p100 fixed the escaped-space half of copyMode only. Evidence: a .de body containing `\. e` makes groff -Tutf8 -man print nothing at all (no warning, the following text line still prints), while bred reduces the escape to "." and then refuses the page as `macro e`. No installed page hits it. Decide whether the refusal is the right policy or whether `\.` should survive copy mode.

items.title: the four session.compaction events are dropped; the reference client draws a compaction item with a running status and streams its summary, bred shows nothing
items.notes: Found by the 2026-11-25 event-union hunt. Reference behaviour (ext/code/lib/opencode/chunks/shared-events-m77rqa4a.js: session.compaction.started inserts {type:"compaction", status:"running", reason, summary, recent}, .delta appends summary, .ended marks it done, .failed records the error). bred has no compaction handling at all (grep compaction outside lib/opencode: only man-parse .Bl -compact). Decide the legacy shape (a message.part.updated part type, or a new event) before writing the red test; a long session compacts and the transcript currently jumps without saying so.

items.title: session.tool.input.delta is dropped; the tool preview only appears when the whole input has arrived
items.notes: Found by the same hunt. Reference: shared-events case "session.tool.input.delta" appends data.delta to tool.state.input while the tool is streaming. translate handles .started and .ended (which parses the JSON) but not .delta, so bred shows a pending tool with no input until it is complete. Decide whether the text preview is worth a legacy event; the .ended text is authoritative, so this is display-only.

items.title: dmsetup(8) splits load|reload into two words around a .BR line ending in \c
items.notes: Measured at c1f2f38a: man-diff --page /usr/share/man/man8/dmsetup.8.gz says 3222 ours / 3221 man, lost 1 ["load|reload"], with ours as "load|" + "reload". Source is `.BR load | \c` followed by `.CMD_RELOAD` (a .de body whose only line is `.BR reload`), after `.BR compact ", " inverted ", " notrunc .` under .HP, and before `.br`. A minimal .BR load | \c + .de CMD_RELOAD + .BR reload DOES join correctly in bred, so the trigger is context-dependent (the preceding .BR line, the .HP, or the macro body shape). Prove the trigger before fixing; p96 fixed the text-line variant and p98 the no-output-macro variant, so check both before changing the join state.

items.title: the loop has no clock it can enforce: put start/deadline/stopNew in the tracked queue, print the budget in status, and refuse a round after stopNew
items.notes: The 2026-11-25 11:51Z run stopped at 12:28 having set a 15:06 stopNew and never read the clock again: the stop condition lived in prose and in an untracked file nothing parsed. The clock moves to doc/loop/queue.json run (tracked, so a fresh session inherits it), bin/loop-clock.mjs holds the pure budget/canStart logic, status prints it, and round refuses after stopNew unless --force. lastRoundMs is recorded so the printed ETA uses a measured round, not a guess.
